statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of public discovery, listing, article, login and 404 archetypes. Authenticated creation, purchase, subscription, settings and account cancellation were not covered because no credentials or transactions were available.

page.framework: Next.js homepage with Nuxt article surfaces

paths.description: Public discovery homepage and content feed, covering navigation, search, responsive feed cards and global delivery.
Trending listing archetype, representing category and ranking index pages.
Public creator article/detail archetype, covering reading, metadata, media and sharing.
Authentication form, covering input assistance, focus, validation and account entry.
Invalid-route recovery path, covering HTTP failure messaging and onward navigation.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains white, and the emulated-media probe reports color-scheme: normal with body background rgb(255,255,255) while prefers-color-scheme: dark matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens, with a deliberate user override if offered.

findings.summary: Navigation and route/state changes have no authored visual continuity.
findings.evidence: The preference/CSS probe found no active animations, no scroll timelines and no authored transition evidence across the homepage and article navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance meaningful same-document or cross-document navigation with View Transitions while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The login input does not expose a visible programmatic focus treatment.
findings.evidence: After focusing the username input, the computed focus probe reported outline: none and box-shadow: none; the component classes also remove focus outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible to provide a high-contrast focus ring without removing the native outline unless an equivalent is supplied.

findings.summary: Empty login submission does not present clear inline recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: Activating the login button with empty fields left focus on BODY and the invalid-state probe found no field validation message, :invalid target, or useful live-region error.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, focus the first invalid field, associate concise errors, and announce them through an appropriate live region.

findings.summary: Homepage loading is slow enough to fail the Core Web Vitals baseline.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 10.3 s, TBT 370 ms, Speed Index 7.5 s and performance 0.59; the trace corroborates FCP around 690 ms while the mobile layout recorded two long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce critical request depth, and profile the LCP element and interaction work against the performance guidance.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a large request and image payload for a feed landing page.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 166 requests and 3,246,381 transferred bytes, including 83 images (1.73 MB) and 58 scripts (1.39 MB); Lighthouse estimates 790 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial feed depth, deliver responsive modern images, and ensure only true critical resources are requested before the first viewport is usable.

findings.summary: Large amounts of JavaScript and CSS are unused during the tested homepage load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 512 KiB unused JavaScript and 21 KiB unused CSS, with 1.8 s JavaScript execution and 3.2 s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route and component code, remove duplicate/legacy payloads, and defer conditional dependencies until their feature is used.

findings.summary: Visible creator labels do not match their accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse axe audit label-content-name-mismatch failed on 40 profile links because the visible name/time text is not included in the aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each accessible name include the visible label text, or remove the overriding aria-label when link text already provides the correct name.

findings.summary: A large first-party JavaScript chunk lacks a production source map.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse valid-source-maps flags _next/static/chunks/87606-cad16c65e603c413.js as a large first-party file without a source map.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps to the error-monitoring/debugging pipeline or expose appropriate maps if policy permits.

findings.summary: The dynamic homepage feed is largely unavailable to non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability evidence found only 10% raw/rendered word coverage: raw HTML had 236 text characters versus 4,433 rendered, and the crawler screenshot showed only a loading indicator. The article archetype itself was server-rendered.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary homepage feed and navigation content so useful links and summaries exist in the initial HTML, then hydrate enhancements.

findings.summary: Transport hardening and cookie policy leave avoidable downgrade and policy gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found HTTPS and CSP, but no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence found three identifier cookies without Secure and several SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and nosniff, set explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and mark all HTTPS-site cookies Secure while narrowing SameSite=None to cases that require it.

findings.summary: The public homepage loads analytics before any demonstrated user choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence identified Google Tag Manager among three third-party origins; the HAR shows the analytics script at about 160 KB and high priority, although DOM evidence confirms it is async.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the purpose and consent basis, minimise collected fields, and delay optional analytics until consent or idle time where required.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface does not offer a passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login screenshot and form probe show Google, X, Apple, email/note ID and password options, with no WebAuthn/passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey authentication and conditional mediation as a progressive option alongside existing account recovery paths.

findings.summary: The homepage’s core discovery content is not progressively enhanced.
findings.evidence: With JavaScript unavailable, the crawler screenshot remains at a loading indicator and raw HTML preserves only 10% of rendered content words, while article content demonstrates that SSR is feasible on the same platform.
findings.suggestedFix: Render meaningful feed entries and navigation server-side, preserving crawlable links and usable fallback states before hydration.

findings.summary: The public content platform is neither installable nor registered for offline handling.
findings.evidence: The DOM found no manifest link, the service-worker registration probe returned an empty list, and no offline surface was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: If repeat reading is a product goal, add a manifest and a small service worker with an explicit offline reading/error fallback; otherwise document this resilience decision.

findings.summary: CSS is not ready for bidirectional layout despite correctly declared Japanese language.
findings.evidence: The DOM reports lang=ja-JP, but stylesheet inspection found 181 physical left/right declarations and only one logical-property rule, making RTL adaptation fragile.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer margin/padding/inset inline/block logical properties and test representative components under dir=rtl.

findings.summary: Feed images are substantially over-delivered and overwhelmingly use legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 63 oversized images, 54 without srcset, 98 legacy-format images and no modern-format images among 100 inspected; HAR attributed 1.73 MB to images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, use sizes/srcset matched to card widths and DPR, and retain intrinsic dimensions and lazy loading.

findings.summary: The content platform exposes no structured agent capability surface.
findings.evidence: The agent probe found no WebMCP registration even though public articles have clear summarisation and discovery value; article JSON-LD is present but is metadata rather than a callable capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider narrowly scoped, user-authorised agent tools for search, reading lists or creator actions, while keeping article metadata crawlable.

findings.summary: Repeated feed traversal grows an already large heap substantially.
findings.evidence: Heap summaries rose from 1,063,081 nodes / 50,219,780 bytes to 1,457,060 nodes / 65,562,296 bytes after ten bottom/top traversals, a roughly 37% node and 31% self-size increase. The evidence does not isolate a detached-node leak, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or cap retained feed items, release stale card state/listeners, and repeat the baseline-target-final heap workflow to distinguish expected cache growth from retention.
